cards.title: What a decision tree is
cards.hook: A decision tree asks one question per node until it reaches an answer.
cards.visual:
PartMeaning
Root nodefirst attribute test (e.g. Patrons?)
Internal nodeattribute test
Branchone value of the attribute
Leafoutput class (WillWait Yes/No)
Decision pathroot → leaf = an if/then rule
formula: classification: entropy/IG or Gini; regression: MSE/variance reduction
example: Restaurant tree: Patrons = None → No; Some → Yes; Full → ask WaitEstimate.
cards.memory: Root asks, branches answer, leaves decide.
cards.trap: Trees overfit when grown too deep: control with max_depth, min_samples_leaf or pruning (ccp_alpha).
explain: A decision tree is a flowchart of questions. You start at the top (root), answer a question about one attribute, follow the branch for your answer, and keep going until you reach a leaf that gives the prediction.
Restaurant example: 'How many patrons?' None → don't wait; Some → wait; Full → ask about the wait estimate, and so on.
Learning a tree means choosing which question to ask at each node. Good questions split the examples into groups that are as 'pure' (all one class) as possible. Entropy and Gini measure that purity.

cards.title: Entropy
cards.hook: Entropy measures how mixed (uncertain) a node is.
cards.trap: Using ln instead of log₂ gives values in nats (max 0.693), not bits.
explain: Entropy measures how mixed up a group is, i.e. how surprised you'd be by a random example's label.
If every example in a node is 'yes', there's no surprise: entropy 0. If it's exactly half yes and half no, you can't guess at all: entropy is at its maximum, 1 bit (for two classes).
Use log base 2, so the answer is in bits. By convention 0 × log₂0 = 0.

where: fraction of examples in class i

cards.hook: Information gain = how much a split reduces uncertainty.
formula: fraction of examples going down branch v
example: Type: every branch 50/50 → weighted entropy 1.0 → IG = 0.
cards.trap: Weight children by size. An unweighted average of child entropies is the #1 IG mistake.
explain: Information gain = how much a question reduces the mixed-up-ness. Entropy before the split minus the (weighted) entropy after.
Weighted means each branch counts in proportion to how many examples go down it: a big messy branch hurts more than a tiny messy one.
ID3 picks the attribute with the highest gain. Patrons: before 1.0, after 0.4591 → gain 0.5409. Type: every branch still 50/50 → gain 0.

where: examples with attribute value v (one branch)
the branch's share of the examples

cards.title: Gini index and Gini reduction (CART)
cards.src: Lecture 4, slides 40-41; Comparing two attributes to split (Type vs Patrons)
cards.hook: Gini asks: if I label randomly by this node's mix, how often am I wrong?
example: Type: all branches 50/50 → weighted Gini 0.5 → reduction 0.
CART binary split Some vs {None, Full}: weighted Gini 0.25, gain 0.25 (Lecture 4 slide 41).
cards.memory: Entropy and Gini agree in spirit: low impurity after the split wins.
cards.trap: Pick the LOWEST weighted Gini but the HIGHEST information gain. Don't mix the directions.
explain: What Gini means: pick one example at random from the node, then guess its label at random using the node's own class proportions. Gini is the probability your guess is WRONG. So Gini measures impurity: 0 means you can never be wrong (pure node); bigger means more mixed.
Why it is 1 − Σp²: the chance your guess is RIGHT is: pick class i (probability pᵢ) AND guess class i (probability pᵢ), summed over classes = Σpᵢ². So the chance of being wrong is 1 − Σpᵢ².

What 'binary max = 0.5' means: with only two classes ('binary'), the worst possible mix is 50/50. Then Gini = 1 − 0.5² − 0.5² = 0.5. That is the largest value Gini can reach with two classes, just as entropy's maximum is 1 bit. (With more classes the maximum is higher, e.g. 1 − 1/3 ≈ 0.667 for three equal classes.)

Using it for splits (CART): compute Gini of each branch, weight by branch size, and add: that's the weighted child Gini. The best split has the LOWEST weighted Gini, i.e. the LARGEST Gini reduction (parent − weighted children).
Patrons: parent 0.5 → weighted children 0.2222 → reduction 0.2778. Type: every branch stays 50/50 → weighted Gini 0.5 → reduction 0. So Patrons wins, agreeing with information gain.

where: fraction of examples in class i
